$comment: The full PaymentStatus transition matrix per spec/02-invariants.md#i2. Rule: a transition from any TERMINAL state (Succeeded, Failed, Canceled, Expired) to any state (including back to itself) is illegal. A transition from any NON-TERMINAL state (RequiresAction, Processing) to any state is legal, since those states exist precisely to lead somewhere else. Every runtime's state machine must reject every pair marked legal: false.
note_on_terminal_self_transitions: A terminal state 'transitioning' to the same terminal state (e.g. a redelivered webhook re-reporting Succeeded) is marked illegal here as an FSM transition, but this is not the same thing as rejecting the redelivery outright; per spec/05-webhooks.md, a runtime must recognize the record is already terminal and short-circuit to a no-op returning the existing result, rather than ever reaching this transition check with an attempt to change already-settled state. This matrix defines what the FSM permits when an update is actually applied; the redelivery case is handled by never applying an update to a terminal record in the first place.

transitions.note: still awaiting the same user action, e.g. re-polled before the user has acted
user completed the required action; provider is now processing
user action led directly to a synchronous success
user action led directly to a synchronous failure
user or integrator canceled before completing the required action
e.g. an OTP attempt failed and a fresh OTP submission is required
still in flight, re-polled with no new information
